meta.title: Natural-Hazard, Catastrophe & Black-Swan Exposure
meta.integrity_note: FEMA National Risk Index (NRI) values for Los Angeles County were NOT read directly from a fema.gov page during this session; they were read from independent republications of the FEMA NRI v1.20 dataset (December 2025). They are therefore recorded in the 'reported' column only, marked UNVERIFIED, and listed on the Flagged for Review page with the official FEMA NRI link for manual confirmation. All other rows on this page were read from an official .gov publisher.
meta.calibration_note: The January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires are the best-calibrated recent black-swan event for this market. Los Angeles County published official loss statistics; they are reproduced below and used as the empirical anchor for the catastrophe scenario in the projection model.

rows.m: Probability that the 60% M6.7 event occurs INSIDE the 2030-2035 lease-expiry decision window
rows.v: 14.2% on a compound-restatement basis (10.0% on a simple linear restatement)
rows.s: U.S. Geological Survey (input); arithmetic derivation documented on the Projection page
rows.n: This is a transparent arithmetic restatement of the official USGS 30-year probability, not a new forecast. Compound: 1 - 0.40^(5/30) = 14.2%. Linear: 60% x 5/30 = 10.0%. Both are shown because USGS publishes a 30-year probability and the restatement method changes the answer. The derivation and its limits are shown on the Projection page.

rows.m: Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zones — regulatory framework
rows.v: Earthquake Fault Zones are delineated by the State Geologist along Holocene-active fault traces, generally with an approximately 500-foot buffer on either side of the trace. Development permits may be withheld until a fault investigation is completed. Sellers must disclose to a buyer if the property lies within an Earthquake Fault Zone.
rows.p: Public Resources Code, Division 2, Chapter 7.5, Sections 2621-2630
rows.s: California Geological Survey (Department of Conservation) — Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zones
rows.n: Disclosure duty under PRC Section 2621.9 attaches on a SALE — directly relevant to the sell-versus-hold decision.

rows.m: Alquist-Priolo — new and revised zones proposed for Los Angeles County
rows.v: Preliminary Review Maps released for public review and comment detailing proposed new and revised Earthquake Fault Zones for Los Angeles County (Antelope Valley), followed by a State Mining and Geology Board public hearing
rows.s: County of Los Angeles / California Geological Survey
rows.n: Shows the regulatory hazard map is still EXPANDING, not static. Detailed maps: https://www.conservation.ca.gov/cgs/preliminary-releases

rows.m: CAL FIRE Fire Hazard Severity Zones — Los Angeles County, Local Responsibility Area
rows.v: Non-Wildland, Moderate, High and Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the Local Responsibility Area were ESTABLISHED IN 2025
rows.s: Los Angeles County Fire Department, Geographic Information Systems Section (official LA County open-data portal)
rows.n: CAL FIRE notes that the previously available FHSZ layers were 1985, 2007 SRA and 2007/2025 LRA, and that remapping is ongoing using new data, science and technology. Source data: https://frap.fire.ca.gov/projects/hazard/fhz

rows.m: City of Los Angeles — Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone
rows.v: Established in 1999 under Los Angeles Municipal Code Section 57.21.07; comprises MOST OF THE HILLY AND MOUNTAINOUS REGIONS of the City of Los Angeles
rows.s: Los Angeles Fire Department, Bureau of Fire Prevention and Public Safety — Fire Zone History
rows.n: Named communities inside the City VHFHSZ include Baldwin Hills, Bel Air Estates, Beverly Glen, Brentwood, Chatsworth, Eagle Rock, Echo Park, El Sereno, Encino, Glassell Park, Granada Hills, HOLLYWOOD, Lake View Terrace, Los Feliz, Montecito Heights, Monterey Hills, Mount Olympus, Mount Washington, Pacific Palisades, Porter Ranch, San Pedro, Shadow Hills, Sherman Oaks, SILVER LAKE, Studio City, Sunland, Sun Valley, Sylmar, Tarzana, Tujunga, West Hills, WESTWOOD and Woodland Hills.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles — brush clearance requirement inside the VHFHSZ
rows.v: Clearance of hazardous vegetation to a total distance of 200 feet from any structure unless otherwise specified by the Chief
rows.s: Los Angeles Fire Department
rows.n: Inspection fee established by the February 1999 amendment.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles — 'Red Flag Day' criteria
rows.v: Winds stronger than 25 mph AND humidity less than 15%
rows.s: Los Angeles Fire Department
rows.n: On Red Flag Days the Fire Department and Department of Transportation remove illegally parked vehicles in posted VHFHSZ locations. This is the official local definition of the weather state that preceded the January 2025 fires.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles Fire Code — Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone provisions
rows.v: Chapter 49, Requirements for Wildland-Urban Interface Fire Areas; Section 4911 sets VHFHSZ-specific requirements for Los Angeles (no open burning or smoking in the zone; zones posted with suitable signs; restrictions on flame devices, travel on firebreaks, and off-road motor vehicle operation without a special permit)
rows.s: Los Angeles City Fire Code (as published through the City's adopted code)
rows.n: Relevant to any change of use, redevelopment or re-tenanting of a site inside a VHFHSZ.

rows.m: Los Angeles County — attribution of the 2025 population loss
rows.v: DOF attributes the county's 64,000-person 2025 loss to 'a combined effect of the Eaton and Palisades wildfires, normal flow to the Inland Empire, and deportations'
rows.s: California Department of Finance, 2026 Estimates E-1 press release
rows.n: Official state acknowledgement that a single catastrophe plus migration policy moved county population.

rows.m: California FAIR Plan — residential policy growth, most recent quarter
rows.v: approximately 16,000 policies added in Q1 2026, about 2.4% growth over the previous quarter
rows.s: California Department of Insurance — press release, May 1, 2026
rows.n: Read from insurance.ca.gov. CDI describes this as 'a substantial slowdown' and 'a leading indicator of the emerging health of the California insurance market'.

rows.m: California FAIR Plan — residential policy growth, comparison period
rows.v: 35,000 to 50,000 policies added per quarter from 2024 through September 2025; approximately 20,000 added between Q3 and Q4 2025
rows.s: California Department of Insurance — press release, May 1, 2026

rows.m: California FAIR Plan — commercial policy count
rows.v: 21,200 rising to 21,464 policies
rows.s: California Department of Insurance — press release, May 1, 2026
rows.n: CDI: 'Commercial policy counts remained relatively stable, increasing only slightly.' Commercial property — the relevant class for this asset — is far less FAIR-Plan dependent than residential.

rows.m: California property-insurance market — insurer participation
rows.v: Two more Top-10 insurers committed to expanding homeowners coverage in California as of May 1, 2026; the full committed list includes Farmers, Mercury, CSAA, USAA, Horace Mann, Pacific Specialty, California Casualty, Travelers and AAA SoCal
rows.s: California Department of Insurance — Sustainable Insurance Strategy press release
rows.n: CDI: insurers covering roughly one-third of California homes sought rate increases of about 6.9%, described as 'far less than the double-digit increases' of recent years.
